key_insight: YoCausal uses temporally reversed real-world videos as natural counterfactuals to test whether video diffusion models truly capture causal dynamics rather than memorizing statistical temporal patterns.
problem_solved: Provides a real-world, zero-cost benchmark to detect causal understanding in video generation models, closing the sim-to-real gap of prior synthetic-only causality tests.
method: Two-level benchmark inspired by Violation of Expectation (VoE): create counterfactuals by time-reversing real videos and measure model responses.
Compare model predictions/likelihoods on normal vs reversed clips to quantify sensitivity to causal violations.
Aggregate metrics across datasets and scenarios to reveal whether models learn causal mechanisms or exploit temporal statistics.
impact: Enables practitioners to reliably evaluate and diagnose causal reasoning in video generative models on real data, guiding development of more robust world models and reducing overfitting to spurious temporal cues.
visual_elements: Side-by-side frames: original video next to its temporally reversed counterpart (example: falling object vs reversed rising motion).
Pipeline diagram: input video → temporal reversal (counterfactual) → model evaluation → causal-sensitivity score.
Bar chart: model scores (normal vs reversed) across multiple VDMs highlighting causal-sensitivity gaps.
Heatmap/timeline: where along a clip models show highest disagreement or failure to detect causal violations.
paper_title: YoCausal: How Far is Video Generation from World Model? A Causality Perspective
paper_authors: You-Zhe Xie, Yu-Hsuan Li, Jie-Ying Lee, Kaipeng Zhang, Yu-Lun Liu
